Carrier Definition Comparison: ACMG-PLP vs ClinVar-PLP

Same genes, same disease mapping, same canonical-denominator method — only the pathogenicity classifier defining "carrier" changes

The main report defines a carrier as someone with an ACMG-PLP variant. This companion report asks: what happens if we instead required ClinVar-PLP confirmation? Answer: it doesn't just lower the numbers — it reproduces the ancestry gap from the concordance finding inside the penetrance denominator itself. Restricting to ClinVar-PLP drops 1,724 carriers overall (45% of the ACMG-PLP carrier pool) across these genes, and (see the main report) that loss falls disproportionately on non-European ancestries — up to 90.9% of ACMG-PLP carriers in EAS have no ClinVar confirmation at all, vs. 42.5% in EUR. This is why the main report's headline penetrance numbers use ACMG, not ClinVar, as the carrier definition.

What "canonical carriers" means, again

Same definition as in process_walkthrough.html: the ONE carrier set per gene, built by raw rows → unique person×gene → restricted to a PLP classification → joined to cohort → sex-restricted if applicable. The only difference between the two columns below is which classification (ACMG-PLP vs ClinVar-PLP) is used in that restriction step — everything else in the pipeline is identical.

Calculation and statistics used

Penetrance — computed separately for the ACMG-PLP carrier set and the ClinVar-PLP carrier set (same formula, different input population):

p̂gene,cancer,age  =  N(carriers with matched cancer)N(all canonical carriers)      [age band, sex-restricted where applicable]

Background (population baseline) rate — same disease and age band, computed over the whole cohort, independent of which classifier defines "carrier":

r̂bg, disease, age  =  N(cohort with that disease)N(cohort in that age band)

Confidence intervals — 95% Wilson score interval on every proportion above (penetrance, background rate, concordance/discordance rate), chosen over the simpler normal approximation because several cells here have small N or proportions near 0/1, where the normal approximation undercoverages and can produce bounds outside [0,1]:

CI  =  p̂ + z2/2n  ±  z√(p̂(1−p̂)/n + z2/4n2) 1 + z2/n

z = 1.96 (95% level), n = denominator count above. Computed via statsmodels.stats.proportion.proportion_confint(method="wilson").

"Significantly elevated" (★) — a non-overlapping-interval test, not a formal two-proportion hypothesis test (no p-value computed):

CIlower(carrier rate)  >  CIupper(background rate)

Carrier-count ratio (last table column) — a descriptive ratio, not a statistical test, used only to rank which genes lose the most carriers under the ClinVar restriction:

ratio  =  NClinVar-PLPNACMG-PLP

Min-carriers thresholds used

Two different thresholds exist in this pipeline:

  • Gene-inclusion bar (20 canonical carriers): a gene needs ≥20 canonical carriers to be treated as "interpretable." This comparison report applies that same bar to both classifiers — ACMG-PLP N and ClinVar-PLP N each need ≥20 — so neither side gets an easier standard. The full table further down still shows every gene, including ones that fail this bar on one or both sides, so the shortfall itself stays visible.
  • Evidence-gap threshold (3 carriers): used only in the ancestry-breakdown table to flag gene×ancestry cells too sparse to trust. Unrelated to this comparison.

Confident genes only

Figures below are restricted to genes meeting both N bars at the same threshold: ACMG-PLP N ≥ 20 and ClinVar-PLP N ≥ 20 (identical value, applied consistently to both classifiers). 15 of 27 genes qualify; the rest are listed in the table at the very bottom with the specific reason each was left out of the figures — nothing is silently dropped, it's just not plotted.

Rows where the last column is well under 100% are genes where switching to ClinVar-PLP would have thrown away a substantial share of real carriers — and, per the main report's concordance finding, that loss is not random across ancestries.

Interpretation

This comparison is not "which number is right" — ACMG-PLP is the carrier definition used throughout the main report, for the reason stated above. It exists to make concrete, gene by gene, what the abstract concordance percentage in Finding 1 actually costs: real carriers who would be excluded from any pipeline that requires ClinVar confirmation before counting someone as a carrier.
